verdicts.reason: A uses a sensible two-column banner layout (can left; headline, tagline and CTA right), but the tagline is almost as large as the headline, the can is small with dead space around it, and the tiny SOLSTICE logo floats off-axis above the text. B is a squeezed copy of the vertical stack: the logo sits stranded in the top-right corner instead of on the centre axis, the headline and tagline are jammed together, and the CTA is pressed against the bottom edge.

A keeps the original centred axis (logo, can, headline, tagline, CTA), but the CTA is shrunk to a small pill with near-illegible label text, so the action is buried, and the tagline competes with the headline. B has a stronger CTA, but the logo is moved off-axis to the top right, the type block is cramped, and the CTA nearly touches the bottom edge.

A scrambles the reading order: the headline is at the top, the can is pushed into the bottom-left corner against the edge, the CTA floats on the right, and the brand logo is demoted to a tiny mark at the bottom, which breaks fidelity and grouping. B keeps the original top-to-bottom order, though its logo is stranded top right and its stack is cramped against the bottom edge.
